units.text: INT. DR. OKAFOR'S OFFICE - CONTINUOUS
A warm room.
Diplomas on the wall.
A box of tissues, strategically placed.
A model of a uterus on the desk that Cal keeps looking at, then looking away from.
DR. OKAFOR, 50s, kind eyes, silver glasses, stands to greet them.
Please, sit. I'm Dr. Okafor. I've read your file. How are you feeling?
units.name: DR. OKAFOR

units.text: Fine! Good. Super.
units.name: BETH

units.text: Fantastic. Never better.
units.name: CAL
paren: sitting, crossing his legs, then uncrossing

units.text: You're both very brave to be here.
units.name: DR. OKAFOR

units.text: We are not. We are very afraid.
units.name: BETH

units.text: We're terrified.
units.name: CAL

units.text: Both speak at once.
It's been three years.
units.name: BETH

units.text: It's been three years.
units.name: ^CAL

units.text: They look at each other.
The room goes quiet for a second.
That is a long time to hope.
units.name: DR. OKAFOR

units.text: Beth's face crumples a little.
Cal takes her hand, and she lets him.
Sorry. I told myself I wouldn't do this.
units.name: BETH

units.text: Everyone does. It's one of the reasons I keep a big box.
units.name: DR. OKAFOR

units.text: The door opens a crack.
TINA, 20s, a nurse in cartoon scrubs, leans in.
Doctor, I'm so sorry. The lab is on the phone.
units.name: TINA

units.text: Excuse me one moment.
units.name: DR. OKAFOR

units.text: She picks up the desk phone.
We hear a faint voice through it.
It's about the samples from last week, Doctor. They've come back.
units.name: TINA

units.text: Thank you, Tina. I'll tell them myself.
units.name: DR. OKAFOR

units.text: She puts the phone down very slowly.
Beth grips Cal's hand so hard his fingers go white.
Is it bad?
units.name: BETH

units.text: Beth. Cal. I think you should both take a deep breath.
units.name: DR. OKAFOR
paren: smiling, for the first time all morning

units.text: Outside, the fish swims once around the tank and stops.
The light in the blinds turns gold.
Is that a yes?
units.name: CAL

units.text: It's a yes.
units.name: DR. OKAFOR

units.text: Beth bursts into tears.
Cal laughs, jumps up, knocks over the model on the desk, and catches it in the air.
Sorry! I got it! I got it!
units.name: CAL
paren: holding it up like a trophy

units.text: Cal, sit DOWN.
units.name: BETH

units.text: He sits.
They hold each other.
Dr. Okafor looks away to give them privacy and quietly dabs her own eyes.
Sunlight.
Quiet.
Somewhere, a baby cries in another room and everyone smiles.
